# SB-1040 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01

Hazard description
------------------
An arc flash event occurred adjacent to the induction power cabinet serving EQ-P3-L2-SB01 during shot blast cabinet maintenance that exposed maintenance personnel to hazard energy. The root cause analysis identified a pattern of uncontrolled residual energy in upstream power components and inconsistent shot media top-up practice resulting in unexpected reconfiguration of the plant interlocks during maintenance. The event produced a localized arc flash that caused a near-miss injury and damaged cosmetic components on the exterior of the induction power cabinet. The primary hazard is exposure to arc flash energy while personnel are performing maintenance or adjustment at the induction power cabinet or associated control panels. Secondary hazards include electrical contact and unintended equipment motion caused by incorrect isolation or discovery of energized conductors during procedures.

Background and rationale
------------------------
EQ-P3-L2-SB01 is operated in a production environment with intermittent access required for maintenance and media handling. Recent inspections, documented maintenance actions, and the related maintenance memo MM-P3-L2-SB01 indicate that routine procedures for media top-up and control logic validation have drifted from best practice. The shot media top-up interval for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 40 hours. When media top-up was deferred or performed outside of the established interval, control routines executed unexpected sequences that altered interlock states at the induction power cabinet. Investigation concluded that two vectors combined to create the hazard: inconsistent administrative controls around when media top-up is performed, and lack of a mandatory lockout-tagout verification step specific to the induction power cabinet prior to any work in the immediate vicinity.

Affected equipment
------------------
- Induction power cabinet adjacent to EQ-P3-L2-SB01.  
- Control panels and local disconnects that serve EQ-P3-L2-SB01 and the Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1.  
- Associated sensors and interlocks that are influenced by shot media level and cabinet operation.  
Personnel working on or near the induction power cabinet during maintenance, media top-up, troubleshooting, or control logic modification are directly affected. Operations staff who perform media top-up activities at the shot blast cabinet are indirectly affected through procedural changes.

Required controls
-----------------
The following controls are mandatory for P3, line P3-L2 operations and maintenance until further revision of the related procedures. These controls are intended to prevent recurrence, provide clear verification steps, and create auditable records.

Administrative controls
- Adhere to MM-P3-L2-SB01 for maintenance coordination and notification prior to any activity that requires access to the induction power cabinet or surrounding enclosures.  
- Update and strictly follow SOP-P3-L2-02 for shot media handling; ensure media top-up is scheduled and documented consistent with the established interval for EQ-P3-L2-SB01.  
- Align troubleshooting and control logic changes with SOP-P3-L2-04; any modification that may affect interlocks requires supervisory authorization and an entry in the change log.

Isolation and verification
- Apply lockout-tagout to power sources that feed the induction power cabinet before any maintenance starts. Tag should reference the specific equipment id EQ-P3-L2-SB01 and the maintenance authorization recorded under MM-P3-L2-SB01.  
- A two-person verification is required: the person who applied the isolation and an independent verifier shall confirm the absence of voltage at points designated in SOP-P3-L2-04 prior to opening interlocked panels or performing work inside the cabinet. Verification must be performed in accordance with SOP-P3-L2-04.

Worksite controls and personal protective equipment
- Establish a controlled work perimeter and use barriers to prevent inadvertent ingress by operations personnel during maintenance.  
- Personnel must use arc-rated protective equipment per the established hazard assessment for the induction power cabinet as defined in site PPE guidance. When performing verification tasks, use insulated tools and test equipment specified in SOP-P3-L2-04.

Operational controls and scheduling
- Schedule shot media top-up activities to occur during planned production pauses or maintenance windows and record each top-up in the media log. Follow the shot media top-up interval for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 40 hours when planning sequences that could influence interlocks.  
- Any unscheduled media top-up or unexpected process behavior must trigger a stop-and-notify protocol coordinated through MM-P3-L2-SB01.

Examples and application
------------------------
Example scenario A: A media top-up is required during an active production run. Before proceeding, operations pauses the relevant line per MM-P3-L2-SB01, maintenance applies lockout-tagout on EQ-P3-L2-SB01 per SOP-P3-L2-04, and two-person verification confirms absence of hazardous energy. Media top-up proceeds following SOP-P3-L2-02. Once complete, reassembly and control logic checks are performed before restoring power.

Example scenario B: A control logic change is proposed that could alter interlock responses. The change is submitted under MM-P3-L2-SB01, reviewed with operations, and implemented during a scheduled maintenance window with lockout-tagout and verification steps documented per SOP-P3-L2-04.

Records to keep
---------------
Maintain auditable records for each activity impacted by this bulletin:
- Media log entries that indicate date, time, personnel, and confirmation that the shot media top-up interval for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 40 hours was observed.  
- Lockout-tagout records and two-person verification forms completed against EQ-P3-L2-SB01. Reference MM-P3-L2-SB01 authorization numbers in the lockout records.  
- Change control records and post-action validations filed per SOP-P3-L2-04 when control logic or interlock behavior is modified.  
- Incident and near-miss reports filed and closed according to MM-P3-L2-SB01.

Effective date
--------------
Effective upon release of Rev E. Continued compliance with this bulletin is mandatory until superseded by a subsequent revision or by procedural changes documented in SOP-P3-L2-02, SOP-P3-L2-04, or MM-P3-L2-SB01.

References
----------
MM-P3-L2-SB01  
SOP-P3-L2-02  
SOP-P3-L2-04
